title: News - European Commission
text:
News (1043)
Businesses and authorities now have an extra eight months — until 1 September 2027 — to prepare for mandatory green-listed waste reporting.
From discovering freshwater biodiversity to learning how to protect water resources, around 500 primary school pupils are taking part in Águeda’s river education programme. Discover how the 2026 European Green Leaf winner is connecting environmental education with local conservation efforts.
From climate research and urban planning to environmental education, Laboratório da Paisagem plays a key role in Guimarães’ journey as European Green Capital 2026. Explore how its work supports local sustainability and inspires collaboration beyond the city.
The restrictions will apply until at least 21 May 2029, after which those nations may apply to receive plastic waste from the EU.
The new rules ban the use and sale of gunshot containing 1% lead or more to protect human health and the environment.
Member State authorities and key stakeholders will discuss challenges and best practices related to large waterbirds.
On 12 November 2026, the Commission adopted measures to restrict lead in fishing weights and lures under the EU’s chemicals legislation, REACH.
In 2024, 2.3 million tonnes of textile waste were generated in the EU. Household disposal accounted for over half of this amount. During the same year, 1.4 million tonnes of textile waste were treated, corresponding to 63% of all textile waste generated that year.
When industry closes down, what’s the best option for the buildings left behind? A study has looked at how circular economy principles have been applied to former breweries, factories and mines in Poland.
Leachate from landfill sites can be detoxified by microbes, including any that are found within. New research explores the factors that influence the composition of these microbiomes, with a view to optimising them as a treatment solution.
